propositions: The code_health metric lens is currently Python-only and hardcodes rebar-specific paths (src/rebar/**/*.py, .github/module-size-limit.txt), making it non-portable to non-Python client projects.
Existing metrics silently fabricate zeros or leak raw FileNotFoundError when scanning absent/unconfigured language paths instead of emitting genuine Unavailable signals, masking portability gaps.
The analyzer must be packaged as an optional [metrics] extra with no hard dependencies in rebar core, allowing core-only installs to gracefully report code_health as Unavailable.

Replace rebar-specific Python readers with a configurable per-project analyzer interface backed by polyglot OSS tools (scc, lizard, jscpd) that return deterministic loc/complexity/duplication signals.
Module-size CAP policy must be decoupled from hardcoded governance artifacts and re-expressed as an optional threshold over a generic LOC signal.
Missing analyzer/tool configuration for a language must emit explicit Unavailable with reason, never fabricated zeros and never raw exception strings.
